acceptance_criteria: Scope-creep check: diff implements exactly the design's :no_task_of_type/:blocked/3 scenario YAMLs/test module, nothing else
Additivity check: REQ-205/206/207's own pre-existing simulation tests independently re-run and confirmed passing unchanged
join_counters defect documented consistently at 3 levels (YAML headers, test module comments, handoff result.issues)
Idiom check on the new runner.ex/scenario_fixture.ex code
Decision-record consistency; blocked_by references ISS-0389 correctly, not a new finding

result.summary:
1) SCOPE CREEP: git diff origin/main...HEAD --stat shows exactly the design's own artefact set -- test/support/simulation/runner.ex (+101/-11), test/support/simulation/scenario_fixture.ex (+/-6), the 3 new scenario YAMLs under test/fixtures/simulation/meridian/scenarios/, test/letflow/simulation/req208_meridian_test.exs, test/reports/req208-meridian-scenario-findings.yaml, plus expected bookkeeping (docs/requirements.yaml status flip pending->in_progress, docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml/v7.yaml append, handoffs/*, docs/anti-patterns.md new entry). No REQ-205/206/207 fixture or test file touched, no lib/ or migration file touched. anti-patterns.md's new entry ('A documented design-doc OQ flagging a real Engine gap can survive its own future requirement untouched...') is itself required by CLAUDE.md's own core-rules ('add to it when you find a mistake worth not repeating') -- not scope creep, a mandated artefact of this exact finding. No unrelated refactoring found anywhere in the diff.

2) ADDITIVITY: independently re-ran (not trusting ELIXIR-DEV's claim) -- `mix test test/letflow/simulation/` = 28/28 passed (REQ-205/206/207/208 combined); `mix test test/letflow/simulation/runner_test.exs test/letflow/simulation/runner_template_and_outcomes_test.exs test/letflow/simulation/seed_idempotency_test.exs` (REQ-205's own pre-existing tests) = 15/15 passed; `mix test test/letflow/simulation/req206_swiftroute_test.exs test/letflow/simulation/req207_vortex_test.exs` included in the 28-pass combined run above, all passing unchanged. `mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force` = clean, exit 0. `mix format --check-formatted` = clean, exit 0. Confirms the design's own additivity claim (§2 preamble: 'every new field/branch defaults to a value that reproduces today's exact behavior when absent') holds in practice, not merely on paper.

3) JOIN_COUNTERS DEFECT DISCLOSURE (3-level check): (a) both loan-origination scenario YAML headers state the defect identically -- same root-cause citation (lib/letflow/engine.ex build_instance_state/3, join_counters: %{} hardcoded, REQ-054/SnapshotWriter serializes but complete_task/3's hot path never reads it back), same consequence statement (scenario truncated to steps 1/2a/2b), same INV-EE48-7/non-crashing-failure characterization. (b) test/letflow/simulation/req208_meridian_test.exs's own header comment (lines ~6-23) and its two 'reproduces the join_counters defect' test names/assertions (lines 558-616, 654-690) restate the identical finding, including the same error tuple ({:activation_failed, {:unknown_branch_id, _}}) and the same real-HTTP-500/INV-4-mapping detail. (c) step-02a-elixir-dev.json's result.issues[0] (BLOCKER severity) states the same root cause, same file/line citations, same 'not fixable within REQ-208's own scope' framing, and step-02c's PASS independently re-confirms the same facts (INV-4 body check, DoS/exposure analysis) match the diff's own evidence. All three levels are consistent -- no level silently works around or downplays what another level discloses. This is the same 'residual risk documented at 3 levels' convention this project already established for ISS-0380/REQ-207.

4) IDIOM CHECK on runner.ex/scenario_fixture.ex: the new :blocked branch in run_steps/1's case dispatch is a plain, flat pattern-match parallel in shape to the existing :skip branch -- no defensive nil-checking beyond the one deliberate fail-loud ArgumentError (mirrors :skip's own missing-severity discipline exactly, same style, same message-format convention: '#{inspect(step)}' interpolation). The new verify_outcome/2 clause for :no_task_of_type is a single `with` chain reusing resolve_ref/3 and fetch_prefix/1 verbatim (no new resolution logic invented) and introduces one small, genuinely-reusable helper (fetch_required/2, generalizing fetch_prefix/1's {:error, {:missing_arg, key}} shape to any key) rather than duplicating that shape inline -- this is a legitimate, minimal, non-anticipatory abstraction (extracted from one concrete duplicated need, not built ahead of a use case). scenario_fixture.ex's two-line change (adding "blocked"=>:blocked to @via_atoms, "no_task_of_type"=>:no_task_of_type to @check_atoms, one maybe_put for :blocked_by) is exactly the closed-vocabulary-atom-table extension pattern REQ-206/207 already established -- no parser logic branch added, consistent with the design's own §1.3 claim. No gen_statem/supervision concerns apply to this diff (test-support harness code, no process/OTP structure touched).

5) SCOPE CREEP (abstraction-ahead-of-need check): the two new primitives (:blocked, :no_task_of_type) are each justified by a concrete, cited gap in the existing closed vocabulary (design §2.1's 'is :skip the same disposition as :blocked -- no' analysis; §2.2's 'does task_assigned support asserting absence -- no' analysis) rather than added speculatively. Neither introduces a new behaviour, macro, or generic plumbing layer -- both are one new atom each in an already-existing closed-enum-dispatch shape. No abstraction found ahead of what REQ-208's own 3 scenarios need.

6) DECISION-RECORD CONSISTENCY: blocked_by is literally "ISS-0389" in the BaFin scenario YAML (test/fixtures/simulation/meridian/scenarios/regulatory-compliance-review-bafin.yaml step 3) -- the already-filed advance-timer gap, not a freshly-invented finding; confirmed docs/issues/ISS-0389.yaml already lists REQ-208 in its own related field per the design doc's own citation (§0.4). No S0 decision record (docs/migration/decisions/) is touched or contradicted by this diff -- no framework/library choice made here.

Type-safety observation (non-blocking, not filed as a new issue): Scenario.step()/RunReport.step_result() remain plain maps with optional keys rather than a discriminated union/struct per via value (e.g. blocked_by required only when via == :blocked is enforced by a runtime ArgumentError, not the type system). This is not a new pattern introduced by this diff -- it is the identical map-based shape REQ-205/206/207 already established and REVIEWER already passed three times over; filing it now as a fresh type-safety issue would misrepresent an already-accepted, load-bearing test-harness convention as a new finding. Noting here for visibility only, consistent with 'worth watching as the schema grows' framing rather than a blocking or freshly-filed gap.

Overall: idiomatic, additive, correctly scoped, consistently disclosed at all 3 levels, and consistent with existing decision records. PASS.
